blocks.x: Achala's Applied AI & Generative AI domain takes AI from promising demo to dependable production. Eight practices span strategy, GenAI platform engineering, retrieval systems and multimodal products — every deployment carrying its own evaluation record and business metric.

The domain covers the full surface where language and prediction models carry enterprise work: strategy that survives procurement, platform engineering that holds under audit, retrieval that cites, tuning that does not regress, and vision and conversational systems wired into the tools staff already use.

Seven practices run under one evaluation discipline. A model change, a corpus change or a prompt change is the same event class, versioned, graded, and gated, because in production they are all just changes to the answer.

blocks.x: What separates a production program from a stalled pilot
blocks.sub: The four program properties we install: eval gates, permission fidelity, cost ceilings, named owners

blocks.x: Language models are commodity infrastructure now; what separates a working program from a stalled one is everything around the model, the corpus, the permissions, the evaluation, the cost line and the surface where staff actually meet the answer.

This domain runs those seven practices as one system. Strategy picks the fights worth having, the platform makes every model call observable and bounded, retrieval and tuning make answers defensible, and vision and conversation put the work inside operational tools rather than another tab nobody opens.

The disciplines are shared across practices: one eval harness, one model registry, one guardrail stack, one cost model. That is what lets a team move from pilot to production without re-earning trust for every new use case.

blocks.x: The evaluation discipline is the product
blocks.sub: Golden sets, calibrated LLM juries and CI gates, why this domain ships reliability instead of demos

blocks.x: Generative programs fail at evaluation, not at generation: models answer everything, so teams stop asking whether the answer is right. The domain standard is an eval harness treated like a test suite, a versioned golden set per use case, LLM-jury scoring calibrated against human-labeled samples, and hard CI gates that block any prompt, model or index change that moves the wrong metric. Jury calibration is the craft: the judge model is scored against human labels every quarter, and its agreement is reported alongside the metric it certifies, because an uncalibrated judge certifies nothing.

The second discipline is permission fidelity. Enterprise retrieval fails quietly when the index leaks a document the asker cannot legally read, so the permission map is folded into retrieval at query time, not filtered after generation, and every answer carries citations to the passages it used. The trace store keeps prompt, context and output for every answer, which turns 'the model said so' into an examinable artifact. That combination, evaluated, permissioned, cited, is what separates a production program from a stalled pilot.

items: Golden sets per use case
Versioned question sets with labeled answers; the bar any release must clear.
Calibrated LLM juries
Judge agreement against human labels reported quarterly, uncalibrated judges certify nothing.
CI gates on every change
Prompt, model or index edits run the harness; regressions block the merge.
Permission-folded retrieval
ACLs enforced at query time; citations prove what the answer saw.
We have a model vendor — what is left for you to build?

The system around the model: corpus engineering, permission-aware retrieval, the eval harness, guardrails, cost controls and the surfaces where staff use the answer. The vendor supplies the model; the program makes it defensible in production.
How do you keep answers from hallucinating?

Grounded generation with citations at query time, permission-folded retrieval so the answer only sees what the asker may read, and an eval suite that scores groundedness per release, regressions block the merge before anything ships.
What does a PoC cost us if it fails?
Four weeks and one practice's slice on your real data path. The exit is a validated metric delta or a written kill memo with reasons, both are deliverables, and neither commits you to a build.
Can fine-tuning be avoided?

Usually at first: retrieval and prompt discipline cover most enterprise needs. Tuning enters when task accuracy against the base model misses the signed bar, and then it ships with drift watch and rollback paths.
Who owns the eval suite after handover?
Your team, with the golden sets, jury calibration schedule and CI gates the build phase installs, the same harness that gated every release during delivery.
